theory.aim: To study the effect of flow pattern on the performance of a heat exchanger.
theory.description: A heat exchanger is a device used to transfer heat between two fluids at different temperatures without mixing them. The performance depends strongly on the flow arrangement. In co-current flow, both fluids move in the same direction. In counter-current flow, fluids move in opposite directions. Counter-current flow generally gives higher effectiveness.
procedure: Select the flow arrangement (co-current or counter-current).
Supply hot and cold fluids to the heat exchanger.
Measure inlet temperatures of hot and cold fluids.
Allow the system to reach steady state.
Calculate the effectiveness of the heat exchanger.

diagnostics.message: Co-current flow generally results in lower effectiveness.
Counter-current flow provides higher heat transfer effectiveness.

viva: Differentiate between co-current and counter-current flow.
Why is counter-current flow more efficient?
Define effectiveness of a heat exchanger.
